geometry_edits.rationale: Preserve the compact host but make the dominant void more explicit and public-facing.
Increase the carved void so the court becomes a clearer spatial organizer.
Strengthen the access-side overhang to improve the street threshold without breaking the compact mass.

graph_edits.rationale: Make the dominant mass less box-like and give the void stronger public legibility while preserving the current primary gesture.
Slightly enlarge the courtyard so the open space reads as a clearer organizing figure and not a shallow notch.
Lower the terrace link to strengthen the ground-threshold relationship and make the access-side seam more evident.

rationale: The candidate reads as one compact stepped mass with a carved central void, and it is coherent across all four views rather than collapsing into a single-view trick. The dominant gesture is legible, the upper volume is secondary to the court, and the silhouette has a real section idea rather than arbitrary terracing. It responds to the parcel in a reasonably contained way instead of merely filling the boundary, and the access edge is acknowledged by a ground-level indentation/porch-like condition rather than a sealed frontage. That said, the void is modest and the road-edge response is not yet strong enough to feel fully public; the form still leans a bit boxy and the section is not as expressive as the better references. Program-fit is acceptable for neighborhood living because the mass suggests mixed-use or community-scale inhabitation with an active threshold and a usable court, but it is not yet a fully convincing neighborhood street building.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More pavilion-like and horizontally open than the candidate; avoid copying the lighter roof character.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Central void/courtyard with an upper connector creates a readable public interior and a compact mass hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger and more distributed than this site; the candidate should stay more compact and not imitate tower/podium scale.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like aggregation around a court can support neighborhood programs when the void is the organizing core.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is more top-heavy and less horizontally legible; don’t over-emphasize boxy stacking.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A strong recessed court and overhang can articulate a public threshold from a compact street mass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is flatter and more horizontally spread; the candidate is more compact and stepped.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A continuous low-rise mass can still host a courtyard when the ground edge remains porous and the roofline varies gently.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more expansive and campus-like; candidate should not become a fragmented multi-wing composition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/bridged neighborhood massing can support a public court and clear circulation hierarchy without losing continuity.

warnings: The access-edge response is present but weak; consider making the frontage cut more explicit toward the verified road edge.
The mass is somewhat box-like in the lower body; a cleaner anchor or more profiled section would improve clarity.
The court is legible but could be enlarged or better connected to the ground to read as truly public.
